chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Stump Evans falls ill, and Cab Calloway wanted Caldwell on alto
summary: Caldwell recommended Stump Evans to Cab but Evans got sick; he had left him on C-melody.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, we've just gone back to Hawk and everything too. He -- well, what about Stump Evans? I mean was he -- I mean -- or did you leave before he sort of made it?

Yeah, I left before 'Cause when Stump Evans Cab wanted me to go on alto, back on alto. I told Cab -- I said a friend of mine in Chicago, Stump Evans, and I said -- couldn't get a better man. I wasn't going to (Unintelligible) switching back to the alto. And -- but Stump had gotten sick. I think he got pneumonia or TB or something like that.
You see, I always thought of him as an alto player said oh no, I never (unintelligible), but Earl Hines (unintelligible).
See, most of these (unintelligible) That's what he had C melody. (unintelligible) played with me on those recordings with me, but Bernie Young --
I had left him there with the C-melody.
